newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN FLUSH MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN FLUSH MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted softer in Wednesday's liquid market, dealers said.
They said the central Reserve Bank did not come into the market to mop up excess liquidity by way of auctioning treasury bills despite a forecast surplus of Z$208 million.
"We're don't know why they didn't come in. The market is (therefore) quite liquid at the moment," one dealer said.
Meanwhile, treasury bills were being sold on the secondary market at 24.65 percent, a touch lower than Tuesday's 24.75 percent but call money was stable at 22 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26 percent, slightly down from 26.5 percent and were also sold half a percentage point easier at 25 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were stable at 25.5 percent (buying) but slipped marginally to 24.7 from 24.75 percent on the selling side.
